\newcommand{\SIR}{\operatorname{S-I-R}}

# Set-up details and utilities
Load required modules. 
Note that `EpidemicsCFTP` is under development, while `FigureUtilities` needs in due course
to be pre-compiled!
```{julia}
using Colors, Compose, DataFrames, Measures
import Cairo, Fontconfig, Gadfly
gf = Gadfly

using EpidemicsCFTP

include("./FigureUtilities.jl")
using .FigureUtilities ;
```

```{julia}
const population = 5 ;
const duration   = 2 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```




# Style choices
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch) ;
```

## Dealing with different kinds of incident
Various types of incident are conveniently abbreviated.
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection
R = Removal   ; C = CRemoval   
I = Infection ; P = PInfection ;
```

# Figure 1
We generate a precise equivalent of Figure 1 of Connor-Kendall (in preparation).

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Graphical representation of unconditioned \(\SIR\) epidemic. There are five time-lines."
```{julia}
duration1 = 15 ; population1 = 5 ;
coordinates1 = UnitBox(0, population1, duration1, -population1,
  leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch) ;
```

Here is the set of innovations:
```{julia}
env_figure1 = Innovation(duration1, 
  A[I(1,2,5),  I(2,1,2),  I(3,1,2),  I(4,2,4),  I(6,3,4),  I(7,2,3),  I(8,1,2), 
    I(8,4,5),  I(9,1,4),  I(11,2,4), I(14.5,3,5)], 
  R[R(3,5),    R(5,1),    R(7.5,5),  R(13,3),   R(14,3)],  C[]) ;
```

```{julia}
initial1= SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
chron1  = chronology(env_figure1) ; states1 = [initial1] # both will be overwritten
traj1, realized1 = evolution_recurse!(states1, AbstractIncident[], duration1, chron1)


flow1 = trajectory_table(duration1, initial1, traj1) ;
print(flow1) ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-nodes1
#| fig-cap: "Nodes used in Figure 1 of Connor-Kendall (in preparation)."
compose_nodes_view(duration1, population1, env_figure1, coordinates=coordinates1)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trajectories1
#| fig-cap: "Trajectories of susceptibles, infectives (brown long dashes), \
#|           removals (grey short dashes)."  
draftfigure1b = plot_trajectories(flow1)
draw(PNG("image/draftfigure1b.png"), draftfigure1b)
draw(PDF("image/draftfigure1b.pdf"), draftfigure1b)
draftfigure1b
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: realized1
#| fig-cap: "@fig-nodes1 plus epidemic and removal curves. Realized incidents have   \
#|           coloured backgrounds and thicker line-widths. Epidemic/removal regions are     \
#|           coloured yellow/brown."
draftfigure1a = compose_epidemic_view(duration1, population1, env_figure1, flow1, initial1, realized1; coordinates=coordinates1)
draw(PNG("image/draftfigure1a.png"), draftfigure1a)
draw(PDF("image/draftfigure1a.pdf"), draftfigure1a)
draftfigure1a
```

# Figure 3
We generate a precise equivalent of Figure 3 of Connor-Kendall (in preparation).

**Caption in draft paper:** 
"Modified graphical representation of \(\SIR\) epidemic, conditioned on removals. ..."
```{julia}
duration3 = duration1 ; population3 = population1 ;
coordinates3 = UnitBox(0, population3, duration3, -population3,
  leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch) ;
```

```{julia}
R[R(1,5),  R(2,4),  R(4,4),  R(7,5)]
```

Here is the set of innovations:
```{julia}
env_figure3 = Innovation(duration3, 
  A[I(0.5,2,5),I(2,1,2),  I(2.5,3,4),I(3,1,3),  I(5,2,4),  I(5.5,3,4),
    I(6,2,3),  I(8,2,5),  I(9.5,1,3),I(10,4,5), I(11,4,5), I(12.5,3,5)],
  R[R(1,5),   R(2,4),  R(4,4),  R(7,5)],
  C[C(3.5,1), C(6.5,4),C(7,3),  C(12,5), C(13,5)]) ;
```

```{julia}
initial3 = initial1
chron3   = chronology(env_figure3) ; states3 = [initial3] # both will be overwritten
traj3, realized3 = evolution_recurse!(states3, AbstractIncident[], duration3, chron3)


flow3 = trajectory_table(duration3, initial3, traj3) ;
print(flow3) ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-nodes3
#| fig-cap: "Nodes used in Figure 3 of Connor-Kendall (in preparation)."
compose_nodes_view(duration3, population3, env_figure3, coordinates=coordinates3)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trajectories3
#| fig-cap: "Trajectories of susceptibles, infectives (brown long dashes), \
#|           removals (grey short dashes)."  
draftfigure3b = plot_trajectories(flow3)
draw(PNG("image/draftfigure3b.png"), draftfigure3b)
draw(PDF("image/draftfigure3b.pdf"), draftfigure3b)
draftfigure3b
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: realized3
#| fig-cap: "@fig-nodes3 plus epidemic and removal curves. Realized incidents have   \
#|           coloured backgrounds and thicker line-widths. Epidemic/removal regions are     \
#|           coloured yellow/brown."
draftfigure3a = compose_epidemic_view(duration3, population3, env_figure3, flow3, initial3, realized3; coordinates=coordinates3)
draw(PNG("image/draftfigure3a.png"), draftfigure3a)
draw(PDF("image/draftfigure3a.pdf"), draftfigure3a)
draftfigure3a
```
